description: A lead employment counsel must approve the final resolution package for a former executive's discrimination claim, including the settlement amount, release protections, employment-record terms, and execution safeguards, with input from insurance counsel and the client liaison.

shared_context.S1: The former executive has demanded $425,000 to resolve the discrimination claim, and mediation is scheduled for next week.
shared_context.S2: The company wants a signed settlement containing a release of employment-related claims and a final separation of the parties.
shared_context.S3: Elena Morris has authority to approve the final resolution package.
shared_context.S4: At the firm's mediation-readiness huddle, Elena routinely takes a round of input from coverage counsel and the client liaison before approving settlement terms.
shared_context.S5: The lead attorney is expected to settle on the resolution package terms and authorized settlement amount within the information surfaced in this huddle; open items requiring further external follow-up, such as carrier authority increases or board funding-gap authorization, should be noted as action items but do not prevent the lead attorney from settling on the package framework.

PF1.text: Daniel reviewed the employment-practices liability policy endorsement and confirmed with the carrier this week that the authorized settlement amount for this huddle is exactly $240,000, the carrier's written authority. Payment requires a broad employment-claims release, no admission of liability, and carrier consent before execution. He has not circulated the coverage confirmation to Elena yet.

PF2.text: During a call with the board chair this week, Marisol confirmed that the company will resolve the dispute only if the agreement provides a neutral reference stating the executive's title and employment dates, includes mutual non-disparagement, and makes the resignation effective exactly June 30. The instruction has not yet been added to the mediation file.

acceptance_conditions: The settlement amount must be exactly $240,000.
The agreement must contain a broad release of employment-related claims.
The agreement must contain no admission of liability.
Carrier consent must be obtained before execution.
The agreement must include a neutral reference identifying the executive's title and employment dates.
The agreement must include mutual non-disparagement.
The resignation must be effective exactly June 30.
The insurance coverage confirmation must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The $425,000 demand and ordinary settlement posture do not establish the insurer-approved terms; PF1 changes the authorized settlement amount to exactly $240,000 and requires the broad release, no-admission language, and carrier consent before execution.

The shared record does not specify the company's required employment-record or conduct terms; PF2 changes the package to a title-and-dates neutral reference, mutual non-disparagement, and a resignation effective exactly June 30.
